abstract: Electronic health record foundation models are evaluated using heterogeneous targets, vocabularies, and adaptation procedures, preventing systematic characterization across model families. We introduce EHRMENEIA (https://ehrmeneia.upc.edu/), a benchmark that provides a multidimensional evaluation framework for next-event prediction, multi-horizon event occurrence, trajectory fidelity and few-shot representation transfer. EHRMENEIA preserves each model's native vocabulary and temporal representation while mapping clinical outputs to shared evaluation objects. Applied to two released clinical checkpoints and two synthetic demonstrations, the framework exposed substantial differences not only in performance but in the clinical questions that could be evaluated from each model--dataset interface. EHRMENEIA introduces a view of benchmarking in which the supported clinical evaluation domain is identified before performance within that domain is interpreted. The framework therefore shifts foundation-model benchmarking from scalar ranking toward characterization of what can, and cannot, be inferred from model outputs.
